6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityClose
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtUnit
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.AbelElement
9	
10	/-!
11	# The field-point comparison of the unit, LIFTED to the sheafified functor `picEt`
12	
13	The (C1)/(C2) campaign is stated on the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff`:
14	
15	* (C1) `PicEtAff.unit_injective` (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1)) —
16	  étale separatedness, unconditional on every affine test algebra;
17	* (C2) `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`, Kleiman
18	  2.5(2)) — effectivity over a section-admitting field test;
19	* their combination `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` — `relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`.
20	
21	But every *representability consumer* meets the honest relative Picard functor through
22	`picEt` / `relPicFunctor`, not through `PicEtAff`: the degree-zero functor `pic0Functor`
23	is a subfunctor of `picEtFunctor`, and the DAT-glue → `K_s` assembly (I-0248,
24	`Picard/PicRepDatum.lean`) needs a representation of the sheafified functor at a
25	separably closed / section-admitting field.  The comparison `PicEtAff.unit` and the
26	functor-level unit `relPicToPicEt` are joined by `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
27	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`): on an affine test, evaluation at the terminal open
28	`picEtAffineEquiv` collapses `relPicToPicEt` to `PicEtAff.unit`.  This file carries the
29	campaign's two theorems across that collapse.
30	
31	## Honest scope
32	
33	Mathematically this is a **conjugation** of the landed `PicEtAff` results by the affine
34	comparison isomorphism `picEtAffineEquiv`, so it introduces **no new mathematical
35	content** and **no new hypothesis** — the field-point equivalence carries exactly the
36	curve-point hypothesis `σ` of `EffectivityClose`.  It is worth landing because the
37	composed statement at the level of the functor the representability headline names was
38	recorded nowhere, and it is the interface between the C1/C2 campaign (output on
39	`PicEtAff`) and the `RepresentableBy` route (input on `picEt`/`pic0`).
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEt_injective` — (C1) at the functor level: the unit
44	  component `relPicToPicEt` is injective at **every** affine test, unconditionally.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section` — the functor-level unit is a group
46	  **isomorphism** `relPic C (Spec K) ≃* picEt C (Spec K)` over a section-admitting field
47	  test, with `relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply` identifying its map with
48	  `relPicToPicEt`.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicToPicEt_bijective_of_section` /
50	  `relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section` — the bijectivity/surjectivity corollaries in the
51	  `Function.` idiom consumers cite.
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false
55	
56	universe u
57	
58	open CategoryTheory Opposite
59	
60	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
61	
62	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
63	
64	noncomputable section
65	
66	/-! ## (C1) at the functor level: injectivity of `relPicToPicEt` -/
67	
68	section injective
69	
70	variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
71	
72	omit [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
73	/-- **`relPicToPicEt` factors through `PicEtAff.unit` by the affine comparison**: on an
74	affine test its value is the affine comparison's inverse applied to the plus-construction
75	unit.  The transported form of `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`. -/
76	theorem relPicToPicEt_apply_eq_symm_unit (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
77	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
78	    relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z
79	      = (picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm (PicEtAff.unit C A z) := by
80	  rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A z, MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
81	
82	/-- **(C1) étale separatedness, functor level**: the unit component `relPicToPicEt` is
83	injective on **every** affine test — unconditional, exactly as `PicEtAff.unit_injective`
84	is.  It is the affine comparison composed with the injective plus-construction unit. -/
85	theorem relPicToPicEt_injective (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] :
86	    Function.Injective (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A)) := fun x y h => by
87	  apply PicEtAff.unit_injective C A
88	  rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A x, ← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C A y, h]
89	
90	end injective
91	
92	/-! ## (C1)+(C2) at the functor level: the field-point isomorphism -/
93	
94	section field
95	
96	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
97	variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
98	
99	/-- **The functor-level unit is a group isomorphism over a section-admitting field test**
100	(Kleiman 2.5, both parts, at the level of the sheafified functor): if the curve admits a
101	`K`-point `σ`, the unit component `relPicToPicEt C (Spec K)` is a `MulEquiv`
102	`relPic C (Spec K) ≃* picEt C (Spec K)`.
103	
104	It is `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` conjugated by the affine comparison
105	`picEtAffineEquiv`; `relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply` records that its underlying map
106	is `relPicToPicEt`, so nothing about the honest unit is lost in the packaging. -/
107	noncomputable def relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
108	    relPic C (overSpec k K) ≃* picEt C (overSpec k K) :=
109	  (PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section C K σ).trans (picEtAffineEquiv C K).symm
110	
111	/-- The field-point isomorphism's underlying map is the functor-level unit
112	`relPicToPicEt` — so it is the honest unit made bijective, not a different arrow. -/
113	@[simp]
114	theorem relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C)
115	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
116	    relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section C K σ z = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z := by
117	  change (picEtAffineEquiv C K).symm (PicEtAff.unit C K z) = relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z
118	  rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt C K z, MulEquiv.symm_apply_apply]
119	
120	/-- **(C1)+(C2) bijectivity, functor level**: over a section-admitting field test the unit
121	component `relPicToPicEt` is bijective. -/
122	theorem relPicToPicEt_bijective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
123	    Function.Bijective (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K)) := by
124	  have h : ⇑(relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K))
125	      = ⇑(relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section C K σ) :=
126	    funext fun z => (relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section_apply C K σ z).symm
127	  rw [h]
128	  exact (relPicToPicEtEquiv_of_section C K σ).bijective
129	
130	/-- **(C2) surjectivity, functor level**: over a section-admitting field test every étale
131	Picard class on `Spec K` comes from an honest relative Picard class. -/
132	theorem relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
133	    Function.Surjective (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K)) :=
134	  (relPicToPicEt_bijective_of_section C K σ).2
135	
136	end field
137	
138	/-! ## The degree of the unit image at the tautological field point
139	
140	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)` is cut out of `picEt C (overSpec k K)` by the vanishing of
141	`degAt` at every field point of `overSpec k K`.  The unit image `relPicToPicEt z` reads its
142	degree at the *tautological* field point — the identity `𝟙 (overSpec k K)` — off the
143	relative degree `relPicDeg K z` of `z` itself.  This is the identity-point instance of
144	`AbelElement.degAt_relPicToPicEt`, isolated because it is the single instantiation the
145	field-test arguments (`Pic0VanishingFieldTest`) consult in the vanishing direction. -/
146	
147	section degree
148	
149	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
150	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
151	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
152	
153	/-- **The unit image's degree at the tautological point is the relative degree**: for
154	`z : relPic C (overSpec k K)`, the degree of `relPicToPicEt z` at the identity field point
155	`𝟙 (overSpec k K)` is `relPicDeg K z`.  The `degAt`-at-identity collapses by `picEtMap_id`
156	and `AbelElement.degAt_relPicToPicEt`'s route (`picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`,
157	`PicEtAff.degAff_unit`). -/
158	theorem degAt_relPicToPicEt_id (z : relPic C (overSpec k K)) :
159	    degAt (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z) (𝟙 (overSpec k K)) = relPicDeg K z := by
160	  rw [degAt_relPicToPicEt (C := C) z (𝟙 (overSpec k K)), relPicMap_id]
161	
162	/-- **A unit image lands in `pic0Subgroup` only if the source has relative degree zero**:
163	membership of `relPicToPicEt z` in the degree-zero subgroup forces `relPicDeg K z = 0`, by
164	testing at the tautological point.  (The converse needs degree vanishing at *every* field
165	point, which is genuinely stronger than degree zero over `K` alone — hence stated in this
166	one honest direction.) -/
167	theorem relPicDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_pic0Subgroup {z : relPic C (overSpec k K)}
168	    (hz : relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k K) z ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) :
169	    relPicDeg K z = 0 := by
170	  have h := (mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mp hz) K (𝟙 (overSpec k K))
171	  rwa [degAt_relPicToPicEt_id] at h
172	
173	end degree
174	
175	end
176	
177	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivitySplice
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityMoving
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityTrivialization
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RelPicCoverInjective
10	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.NormalizedComparisonExists
11	
12	/-!
13	# The (C2) effectivity theorem and the surjectivity close
14	
15	**The campaign close.**  The fppf-effectivity theorem of the (C2) campaign (Kleiman,
16	*The Picard Scheme*, `th:cmp` Part 2 recast on the cocycle model) and the resulting
17	bijectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction over section-admitting field
18	tests:
19	
20	* `Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces` — effectivity for an arbitrary
21	  faithfully flat `A → B`, given a covering family of trivialized pieces: a rigidified
22	  class on the cover curve whose two coprojection pullbacks agree on the nose descends
23	  along the cover inclusion `cg`.  The σ-normalized comparison exists unconditionally
24	  (E1); flat trivializations come from the trivialized pieces by localize-and-flatten;
25	  the refinement splice assembles the descent.
26	* `Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq` — **the (C2) effectivity theorem** for a
27	  module-finite faithfully flat cover: the covering family of trivialized pieces is
28	  produced *unconditionally* by the moving lemma
29	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.EffectivityMoving`).  Module-finiteness is honest: for a
30	  merely quasi-finite étale cover the bare restricted class need not trivialize on any
31	  saturated piece (see the moving lemma's docstring); the close below reaches arbitrary
32	  étale covers of a field test through the field cofinality of étale covers.
33	* `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section` — **the headline**: over a field test `K`
34	  admitting a curve point `σ : Spec K ⟶ C`, the unit of the étale plus construction is
35	  surjective.  A plus class is represented on a finite separable field-extension cover
36	  (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`); the rigidification layer
37	  (G1 + the rigidified transport keystone) puts the representative in the effectivity
38	  theorem's hypotheses; the descended class maps to the original by `mk`-calculus.
39	* `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` — with the (C1) injectivity (étale separatedness),
40	  the unit is a group isomorphism `relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`.
41	-/
42	
43	set_option autoImplicit false
44	
45	universe u
46	
47	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
48	  TopologicalSpace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
49	
50	open scoped TensorProduct
51	
52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
53	
54	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
55	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
56	variable [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
57	
58	section effectivity
59	
60	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B]
61	  [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower k A B]
62	
63	set_option quotPrecheck false in
64	local notation "XA" => (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left
65	set_option quotPrecheck false in
66	local notation "XB" => (C ⊗ overSpec k B).left
67	set_option quotPrecheck false in
68	local notation "u₁" => (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (tensorInl (A := A) (B := B))).left
69	set_option quotPrecheck false in
70	local notation "u₂" => (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (tensorInr (A := A) (B := B))).left
71	set_option quotPrecheck false in
72	local notation "cg" => (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k)).left
73	
74	namespace Over
75	
76	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] (σ : overSpec k A ⟶ C)
77	
78	/-- **(C2) effectivity from a covering family of trivialized pieces** (arbitrary
79	faithfully flat cover): a class on the cover curve represented by `γ`, rigidified along
80	the base-changed section and with equal coprojection pullbacks on the nose, descends
81	along `cg` — provided every point of the base curve lies in an affine piece on which
82	the representing cocycle trivializes. -/
83	theorem exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces
84	    (𝒩 : (XB).PointedCover) (γ : (XB).unitsCocycle 𝒩)
85	    (hrig : Over.IsRigidified
86	      (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ)
87	      (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class))
88	    (hdesc : Scheme.CechPic.map (u₁) (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class)
89	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (u₂) (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class))
90	    (hpieces : ∀ x : XA, ∃ (V : (XA).Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V), x ∈ V ∧
91	      Nonempty (PieceTrivialization C 𝒩 γ V)) :
92	    ∃ M : (XA).CechPic,
93	      Scheme.CechPic.map (cg) M = Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class := by
94	  obtain ⟨W⟩ := exists_normalizedCechComparison C σ 𝒩 γ hrig hdesc
95	  refine exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_flat C σ W fun x => ?_
96	  obtain ⟨V₁, hV₁, hxV₁, ⟨T₁⟩⟩ := hpieces x
97	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, T, hT⟩ :=
98	    exists_flat_pieceTrivialization_of_le C σ W hV₁ T₁ hxV₁
99	  exact ⟨V, hV, hxV, T, hT⟩
100	
101	/-- **The (C2) effectivity theorem** (recon §0.3; Kleiman `th:cmp` Part 2, the descent
102	of the rigidified pair): for a module-finite faithfully flat cover `A → B` of the test
103	algebra of a curve point `σ`, every Čech Picard class on the cover curve `X_B` that is
104	rigidified along the base-changed section (`hrig`) and has equal coprojection pullbacks
105	on the curve over `B ⊗[A] B` (`hdesc`) descends along the cover inclusion:
106	`∃ M, cg^* M = L`. -/
107	theorem exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq [Module.Finite A B]
108	    (L : (XB).CechPic)
109	    (hrig : Over.IsRigidified
110	      (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ) L)
111	    (hdesc : Scheme.CechPic.map (u₁) L = Scheme.CechPic.map (u₂) L) :
112	    ∃ M : (XA).CechPic, Scheme.CechPic.map (cg) M = L := by
113	  induction L using Scheme.CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒩 a
114	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ
115	  rw [show (Quot.mk _ γ : (XB).unitsH1 𝒩)
116	    = CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.class γ from rfl] at hrig hdesc ⊢
117	  refine exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces C σ 𝒩 γ hrig hdesc fun x => ?_
118	  obtain ⟨V, hV, hxV, h1⟩ := Over.exists_isAffineOpen_cechPicMap_preimage_eq_one
119	    (B := B) C (Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒩 γ.class) x
120	  exact ⟨V, hV, hxV, Over.pieceTrivialization_of_cechPicMap_eq_one C V h1⟩
121	
122	end Over
123	
124	end effectivity
125	
126	/-! ## The surjectivity close (recon §0.2) -/
127	
128	section close
129	
130	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
131	
132	/-- **Surjectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction over a section-admitting
133	field test** (Kleiman 2.5(2), axiom (C2) — the campaign headline): if the curve admits
134	a `K`-point `σ`, every class of `PicEtAff C K` comes from a relative Picard class.
135	
136	A representative on an étale cover of `Spec K` is refined to a finite separable field
137	extension (field cofinality); the rigidification layer produces a rigidified Čech
138	representative whose descent equation holds on the nose; the (C2) effectivity theorem
139	descends it along the cover inclusion; and the `relPicMk`/`mk`-calculus identifies the
140	descended class's unit with the original plus class. -/
141	theorem PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
142	    Function.Surjective (PicEtAff.unit C K) := by
143	  intro q
144	  induction q using PicEtAff.ind with | _ E x
145	  classical
146	  -- ### refine the representing cover to a finite separable field extension
147	  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hLalg, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨f⟩⟩ :=
148	    E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
149	  set F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L with hF
150	  set g : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] F.Carrier :=
151	    ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom).comp f with hg
152	  set y : descentClasses C F := descentMap C g x with hy
153	  have hq : PicEtAff.mk C E x = PicEtAff.mk C F y :=
154	    (PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C g x).symm
155	  haveI : Module.Finite K F.Carrier :=
156	    Module.Finite.equiv (R := K) (M := L)
157	      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toLinearEquiv
158	  -- ### a rigidified representative of the descent class (G1)
159	  obtain ⟨Lc, hrig, hLcrep⟩ := relPic.exists_isRigidified_rep
160	    (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ)
161	    (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
162	  have hmem : relPicMk C (overSpec k F.Carrier) Lc ∈ descentClasses C F := by
163	    rw [hLcrep]
164	    exact y.2
165	  -- ### the on-the-nose descent equation (the rigidified transport keystone)
166	  have hdesc0 := Over.IsRigidified.cechPicMap_doubleInl_eq_doubleInr σ hmem hrig
167	  have hinl : doubleInl (k := k) F = tensorInl (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
168	    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
169	  have hinr : doubleInr (k := k) F = tensorInr (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
170	    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
171	  rw [hinl, hinr] at hdesc0
172	  -- ### the effectivity theorem
173	  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq C σ Lc hrig hdesc0
174	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M, ?_⟩
175	  -- ### the `mk`-calculus close
176	  rw [PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C F (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M)]
177	  rw [hq]
178	  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C F) (Subtype.ext ?_)
179	  change relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
180	      (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M) = (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
181	  rw [relPicAlgMap, relPicMap_mk, hM, hLcrep]
182	
183	/-- **The unit of the étale plus construction is an isomorphism over a
184	section-admitting field test** — étale separatedness (C1) plus effectivity (C2):
185	`relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`. -/
186	noncomputable def PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
187	    relPic C (overSpec k K) ≃* PicEtAff C K :=
188	  MulEquiv.ofBijective (PicEtAff.unit C K)
189	    ⟨PicEtAff.unit_injective C K, PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section C K σ⟩
190	
191	end close
192	
193	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# A DEGREE-ZERO PICARD CLASS ON `ℙ¹_K` IS TRIVIAL, FOR EVERY FIELD EXTENSION `K/k`
12	
13	`RiemannRoch/GenusZeroDegreeTrivial.lean` proves `classDeg K L = 0 → L = 1` from `χ(𝒪_X) = 1`
14	at an abstract curve `X` over `K`.  This file instantiates it at `ℙ¹`, which needs `χ = 1` at
15	the *base-changed* curve for every extension `K/k` rather than only over the base field.
16	
17	**READ THE STATUS NOTE BELOW BEFORE CITING THIS FILE.**  An earlier version of this paragraph
18	attributed the "not instantiated at any concrete curve" observation to a note *inside*
19	`GenusZeroDegreeTrivial.lean`.  That is **false** — grep finds no such phrase there, at the
20	commit that wrote it or at HEAD.  The observation came from inbox `I-1616`, a message from the
21	lane that wrote that file, and a docstring is the wrong place to have laundered an inbox
22	message into a citation.
23	
24	## STATUS: this file is a COROLLARY LAYER, not an independent result

26	Measured by a fresh-context audit (`I-1633`), and it is the honest framing: **all four
27	declarations below follow from `Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean` alone**, which landed

29	of that file's `chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero` to
30	`P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero`; I re-verified the subsumption myself rather than take it on report.
31	
32	What is genuinely not duplicated is `eq_of_classDeg_eq_baseChange` — no
33	`Injective (classDeg …)` statement exists elsewhere in the tree — and the value of the rest is
34	that the specialisation at `ℙ¹` is spelled out where a reader of the `ℙ¹` material will find it.
35	That is a convenience, and it should not be quoted as new mathematics.
36	
37	## Why the base-changed curve and not just `ℙ¹_k`
38	
39	The consumer is the `∀ T` binder of the `pic⁰` vanishing.  `pic0Subgroup C T` is cut out by
40	`degAt` at *every field point* `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` (`Picard/Pic0Functor.lean:107`), and
41	`degAt` is read through `relPicDeg K` on `relPic C (overSpec k K)`, which is a quotient of
42	`CechPic ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left)` — the Čech Picard group of the curve base-changed to `K`.
43	So the field-point content of the vanishing is a statement about `ℙ¹_K` for every `K`, and a
44	computation over `k` alone does not touch it.
45	
46	## The composite, and where each input comes from
47	
48	`genus (baseChangeBundle C K) = genus C` is base-field invariance of the genus
49	(`Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean:373`), and `χ(𝒪) = 1 - genus`
50	(`RiemannRoch/ChiCurve.lean:148`).  At `C = P1.asOver k` the genus is `0`
51	(`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean:187`), so `χ = 1` at `ℙ¹_K` for **every** `K`.  Feed that to
52	`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`.
53	
54	Nothing here is new mathematics; all four inputs were landed and unconnected.  The reason it
55	was worth a file is that the composite is what turns a theorem about an abstract curve
56	carrying a `χ` hypothesis into a fact about an object this project has built.
57	
58	## What this does NOT do
59	
60	It does **not** discharge `∀ T : Over (Spec k), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) T)`,
61	and the gap is not a quantifier shuffle.  `pic0Subgroup C T` at a general test `T` consists of
62	classes on `C ⊗ T` whose restriction to every *field* point has degree zero; this file says
63	each of those restrictions is trivial, which is **fibrewise triviality**, not triviality.
64	Concluding the class itself is trivial is the descent step — for `T = overSpec k A` it is
65	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) ≅ Pic(A) × ℤ`, cohomology and base change — and it is untouched here.
66	
67	Recorded because the distance is easy to misread: the field case being closed makes the ring
68	case look like bookkeeping, and it is not.  In particular a chart-by-chart argument does not
69	extend from fields to rings, and the reason is worth separating into what is measured here and
70	what is quoted from outside:
71	
72	* **measured.** `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial k))` is `inferInstance` for a *field*
73	  `k` (through `NormalizedGCDMonoid`), which is what makes the charts of `ℙ¹_k` have trivial
74	  Picard group.  The same query for a general `[CommRing A]` **fails**, and it fails even
75	  given `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)` as a hypothesis.  So the instance that carries the
76	  field argument is simply absent over a ring.
77	* **measured.** `grep -rli` over all of mathlib returns **zero** files matching `seminormal`
78	  and zero matching `traverso`; the `suslin` hit is Suslin's theorem in descriptive set
79	  theory, and every `quillen` hit is the model-structure Quillen.  So no route through that
80	  literature is available in the library as it stands.
81	* **quoted, not verified here.** That `Pic(A[t]) = Pic(A)` holds *exactly* for seminormal `A`
82	  is Traverso–Swan, mathematics from outside this formalization.  Nothing in this tree proves
83	  it or its failure, and the sentence is here to explain why the instance search above is not
84	  merely missing a lemma — not as a formalized no-go.
85	
86	## Main declarations
87	
88	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.chi_baseChange_eq_one` — `χ(𝒪) = 1` on `ℙ¹_K` for every field
89	  extension `K/k`.
90	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange` — **a degree-zero Čech Picard
91	  class on `ℙ¹_K` is trivial**, and `classDeg_eq_zero_iff_baseChange`, the iff.
92	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.eq_of_classDeg_eq_baseChange` — the degree determines the class, which
93	  is the shape a degree-cut-out subgroup consumes.
94	-/

102	
103	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
104	
105	namespace P1

107	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
108	
109	/-- **`χ(𝒪) = 1` on `ℙ¹_K`, for every field extension `K/k`.**
110	
111	`χ = 1 - genus` at any curve, and the genus is a base-field invariant, so this is
112	`genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` transported along `K/k`.  This is the input
113	`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one` needs and the one its author flagged as not
114	elaborated at a concrete curve. -/
115	theorem chi_baseChange_eq_one :
116	    Sheaf.chi (((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 := by
117	  haveI : IsProper (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).hom :=
118	    instIsProperSndLeft (P1.asOver k) K
119	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).hom :=
120	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft (P1.asOver k) K
121	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).hom :=
122	    instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft (P1.asOver k) K
123	  have hg : genus (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K) = genus (P1.asOver k) :=
124	    genus_baseField (P1.asOver k) K
125	  have h0 : genus (P1.asOver k) = 0 := P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k
126	  have hchi := chi_moduleKSheaf (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K)
127	  rw [hg, h0] at hchi
128	  -- `(baseChangeBundle C K).left` is `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` by `rfl`; the two spellings
129	  -- differ only in which one typeclass resolution keys the `Over` instance on.
130	  change Sheaf.chi ((baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).left.moduleKSheaf K) = 1
131	  simpa using hchi
132	
133	/-- **A degree-zero Čech Picard class on `ℙ¹_K` is trivial**, for every field extension
134	`K/k`.
135	
136	The instantiation `GenusZeroDegreeTrivial` was missing: its `χ(𝒪_X) = 1` hypothesis is
137	discharged at this carrier by `chi_baseChange_eq_one`. -/
138	theorem eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange
139	    (L : ((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic)
140	    (hL : classDeg K L = 0) : L = 1 :=
141	  eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one K (chi_baseChange_eq_one k K) L hL
142	
143	/-- The iff, so `classDeg` is visibly **injective** on `CechPic (ℙ¹_K)` rather than merely
144	having trivial kernel on the nose. -/
145	theorem classDeg_eq_zero_iff_baseChange
146	    (L : ((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
147	    classDeg K L = 0 ↔ L = 1 :=
148	  ⟨eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange k K L, fun h => by rw [h, classDeg_one]⟩
149	
150	/-- **The degree determines the class on `ℙ¹_K`**: two Picard classes of the same degree are
151	equal.  (Injectivity of `classDeg`, stated on the multiplicative Picard group rather than on
152	`Additive`, which is the spelling every consumer in this tree uses.)
153	
154	This is the form the degree-zero *subgroup* consumes: `pic0Subgroup` is cut out by a degree
155	condition, and a subgroup lying in the kernel of an injective homomorphism is trivial. -/
156	theorem eq_of_classDeg_eq_baseChange
157	    (L L' : ((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic)
158	    (h : classDeg K L = classDeg K L') : L = L' := by
159	  have hdiv : classDeg K (L * L'⁻¹) = 0 := by
160	    rw [classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, h]
161	    omega
162	  exact mul_inv_eq_one.mp (eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange k K _ hdiv)
163	
164	end P1

136	/-- Every étale cover of a subsingleton ring has subsingleton carrier: the carrier's spectrum
137	maps **onto** `Spec A`, which is empty, so the carrier's spectrum is empty too. -/
138	theorem Algebra.EtaleCover.subsingleton_carrier {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Subsingleton A]
139	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) : Subsingleton E.Carrier := by
140	  haveI : IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum A) :=

146	/-- **The relative Picard group is trivial over a subsingleton test ring.**
147	
148	`Spec A` is empty, so the product `C ⊗ overSpec k A` is empty (project along `snd`), so its
149	Čech Picard group is trivial by the landed `Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`; the

153	theorem subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
154	    [Subsingleton A] : Subsingleton (relPic C (overSpec k A)) := by
155	  haveI : IsEmpty ↥((overSpec k A).left) := by
156	    change IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum A)

163	    induction y using relPic.ind with | mk M =>

169	def toSubsingletonAlgHom (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (R S : Type u)
170	    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra A R] [Algebra A S] [Subsingleton S] :
171	    R →ₐ[A] S where

189	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
190	    [Subsingleton A] : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by
191	  refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩

193	  induction y using PicEtAff.ind with | _ F ζ =>

195	  haveI : Subsingleton (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
196	    subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton C E.Carrier

201	/-- The `pic⁰` form at a subsingleton test ring: a subgroup of a subsingleton group. -/
202	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_subsingleton
203	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
204	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Subsingleton A] :
205	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by

276	The reductions above take the covering family as an argument, which is the wrong interface for

301	theorem span_eq_top_of_forall_prime {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type*} (f : ι → A)
302	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ i, f i ∉ p.asIdeal) :
303	    Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ := by

308	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
309	
310	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION**: if every prime of `A` has *some* basic open neighbourhood on

312	
313	No covering family in the statement: the witnesses are chosen at the primes, shown to span,
314	cut down to a finite subfamily by `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`, and fed to
315	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away`.  The hypothesis is about `Localization.Away f`, a BASIC OPEN and

319	weaker thing than the header of this file originally claimed. -/
320	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime
321	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
322	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
323	    Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by

326	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
327	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime f fun p => ⟨p, hf p⟩
328	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan

332	      ext x; exact ⟨fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => hi ▸ i.2, fun hx => ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩⟩]

342	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by

344	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime C h
345	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
346	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
347	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
348	
349	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION, rigidity spelling**: the `hrigAff` clause at a basic open around
350	each prime gives it at `A`.
351	
352	Same three steps as `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` (choose, span, cut to finite), fed
353	to `PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away`.  Stated separately because `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
354	consumes the rigidity clause and not a `Subsingleton`, and because the rigidity form is the one
355	that carries no degree apparatus. -/
356	theorem PicEtAff.rigidity_of_forall_prime
357	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
358	      ∀ q : PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f),
359	        (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] K),
360	          PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
361	    (q : PicEtAff C A)

363	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) :
364	    q = 1 := by

9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
11	
12	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
13	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
14	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
15	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
16	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
17	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
18	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
19	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
20	
21	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
22	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
23	of the challenge statement file.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
28	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
30	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
31	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
32	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
34	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
36	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
37	-/
38	
39	set_option autoImplicit false
40	
41	universe u
42	
43	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
44	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
47	
48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
53	along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
54	def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
55	  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range
56	
57	lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
58	    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
59	  Iff.rfl
60	
61	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
62	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
63	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
64	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T
65	
66	noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
67	  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)
68	
69	/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
70	noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
71	    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
72	  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)
73	
74	lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
75	    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
76	  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)
77	
78	/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
79	relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
80	lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
82	    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
83	  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem
84	
85	@[elab_as_elim]
86	theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
87	    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
88	    motive x :=
89	  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk

31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a

11	
12	For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the Wave-5 tangent lane built both halves of
13	the two-chart comparison
14	
15	```
16	Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)  ↪  X.CechPic
17	```
18	
19	— surjectivity onto the chart-trivial classes (`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_surjOn_of_chartTrivial`,
20	`Tangent/TwoChartRepresentable.lean:301`) and the exact kernel
21	(`Scheme.twoChartClassHom_eq_one_iff`, `Tangent/TwoChartCechPic.lean:321`).  Composing them
22	gives a **criterion** nobody had stated: if every overlap unit is a coboundary, then every class
23	trivial on both charts is trivial.
24	
25	That composite is what a computation of `Pic` on a two-chart cover actually wants to consume: it
26	turns a statement about the *unit groups of three rings* — pure commutative algebra, no
27	cohomology — into triviality of a Picard class.  Both inputs are general in the scheme, so this
28	is too: no affineness, no curve, no dual numbers, no field.
29	
30	## Why it is here rather than in `Tangent/`
31	
32	The two inputs were built for the Wave-5 `ε`-kernel computation and live there.  This file is
33	about the *Picard group of a two-chart scheme* rather than about tangent spaces, and its intended
34	consumer is the ring-case obligation of the representability route
35	(`Picard/Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean`), where the relevant `X` is a relative curve over a test ring
36	and the three rings are the two chart algebras and their overlap.

43	(`Tangent/TwoChartHonest.lean:108`) derives it from `¬ IsAffine X` alone, and a proper

46

49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.cechPic_eq_one_of_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the
50	  criterion.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subsingleton_chartTrivial_of_overlapUnits_coboundary` — the same as a
52	  statement about the subgroup of chart-trivial classes, for a consumer holding two classes

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.SectionsBaseChange
8	
9	/-!
10	# The canonical section of `ℙ¹` over an arbitrary test ring
11	
12	`ℙ¹` has a canonical rational point — the origin `[1 : 0]` of the first standard chart — and
13	that point exists over *every* base, not only over a separably closed field.  This file packages
14	it as a **section functor**: for every commutative `k`-algebra `A` a morphism
15	
16	  `P1.overSection k A : overSpec k A ⟶ (P1.asOver k)`
17	
18	in `Over (Spec k)`, natural in `A` (`P1.overSection_naturality`).  It is `[1 : 0]` through the
19	chart `D₊(X₀)`, built from `P1Points.fromSpecChart` with the constant chart coordinate `0`; the
20	over-`k` condition is `fromSpecChart_structureMap`.
21	
22	## Why this is worth a file
23	
24	The representability route reaches `ℙ¹` through
25	`AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` and the section-conditional
26	étale↔Zariski comparison
27	`AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section` / `relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section`
28	(`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean`, `Picard/PicEtUnitFieldComparison.lean`).  Both of those
29	consume a section `σ : overSpec k _ ⟶ C` of the curve.  The inbox pricing `I-1603` records that
30	this input — "a `k`-rational point at `ℙ¹`" — **is not constructed anywhere in this project**,
31	even though `ℙ¹` has one over any ring.  This file constructs it, unconditionally on the base
32	field and over an arbitrary test ring, so the comparison lemmas can be instantiated at `ℙ¹`.
33	
34	Nothing here is new mathematics: it is the origin of a chart.  The value is that the section a
35	dozen downstream lemmas assume as a hypothesis now exists as a term, at the object the headline
36	is about.
37	-/
38	
39	set_option autoImplicit false
40	
41	universe u
42	
43	open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory
44	
45	open scoped CartesianMonoidalCategory
46	
47	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
48	
49	namespace P1
50	
51	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
52	
53	/-- The canonical `A`-point `[1 : 0]` of `ℙ¹`, as a morphism `Spec A ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k`.
54	
55	It is `fromSpecChart` through the first chart `D₊(X₀)` with chart coordinate `0`, i.e. the origin
56	of that chart.  Being through a chart it is defined for every ring, with no positivity,
57	separable-closure or nonemptiness hypothesis. -/
58	noncomputable def specPoint : Spec (.of A) ⟶ P1 k :=
59	  fromSpecChart k (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) 0 (0 : A)
60	
61	/-- `specPoint` is a morphism over `k`: composing with the structure map of `ℙ¹` gives the
62	structure map `Spec A ⟶ Spec k` of `overSpec k A`. -/
63	theorem specPoint_structureMap :
64	    specPoint k A ≫ structureMap k = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A)) := by
65	  rw [specPoint, fromSpecChart_structureMap]
66	
67	/-- **The canonical section of `ℙ¹` over the test ring `A`**: `[1 : 0]` as a morphism
68	`overSpec k A ⟶ (P1.asOver k)` in `Over (Spec k)`.
69	
70	This is the section `σ` that `PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section`, `relPicToPicEt_surjective_of_section`
71	and the challenge-target chain all take as a hypothesis; it exists at every test ring. -/
72	noncomputable def overSection : overSpec k A ⟶ (P1.asOver k) :=
73	  Over.homMk (specPoint k A) (specPoint_structureMap k A)
74	
75	@[simp]
76	theorem overSection_left : (overSection k A).left = specPoint k A := rfl
77	
78	/-! ## The global `k`-rational point
79	
80	The monoidal unit `𝟙_ (Over (Spec k))` is *definitionally* `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))` (this first
81	step is `rfl`), so the section at the test ring `A = k` is a **global `k`-rational point**
82	`𝟙_ ⟶ (P1.asOver k)`.  Note the source is `Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`, which is only
83	*propositionally* — not definitionally — equal to `overSpec k k = Over.mk (Spec.map (algebraMap
84	k k))`: matching the two structure maps costs `Spec.map_id` and `algebraMap k k = id`.  That is
85	why the `w`-condition below is discharged by an explicit rewrite rather than by `rfl`.  This is
86	the `P : 𝟙_ ⟶ P1.asOver k` that `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` and the challenge target
87	`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` record as constructed nowhere in the project. -/
88	
89	/-- **The global `k`-rational point of `ℙ¹`**: the origin `[1 : 0]`, as a morphism from the
90	monoidal unit of `Over (Spec k)`.  This is the point hypothesis `P` of the challenge's
91	`JacobianData.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` at `ℙ¹`. -/
92	noncomputable def unitPoint : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ (P1.asOver k) :=
93	  Over.homMk (specPoint k k) (by
94	    change specPoint k k ≫ structureMap k = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
95	    rw [specPoint_structureMap,
96	      show (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k)) = 𝟙 (CommRingCat.of k) from by ext x; simp,
97	      Spec.map_id])
98	
99	@[simp]
100	theorem unitPoint_left : (unitPoint k).left = specPoint k k := rfl
101	
102	/-! ## Naturality
103	
104	The point `[1 : 0]` is *constant*: it does not depend on the test ring, only on `ℙ¹`.  So
105	base-changing the section along an algebra map `A → B` lands on the section at `B`.  Stated at
106	the scheme level (`specPoint_naturality`) it needs no `Over`-category machinery, so this file
107	stays below the Picard layer that owns `Over.overSpecMap`. -/
108	
109	variable (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
110	
111	/-- **Naturality of the canonical point** at the scheme level: pulling `specPoint` back along
112	`Spec` of the algebra map `A → B` is `specPoint` at `B`.
113	
114	`fromSpecChart` is natural in the ring (`SpecMap_fromSpecChart`), and the chart coordinate is the
115	constant `0`, which the algebra map sends to `0`; the base map `k → B` factors as `k → A → B` by
116	the scalar tower. -/
117	theorem specPoint_naturality (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) :
118	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ specPoint k A = specPoint k B := by
119	  rw [specPoint, specPoint, SpecMap_fromSpecChart]
120	  congr 1
121	  · rw [← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
122	    congr 1
123	    exact φ.comp_algebraMap
124	  · exact map_zero _
125	
126	end P1
127	
128	end AlgebraicGeometry
